Required: VK_KHR_swapchain (only when presenting; the headless test path does not need it) and VK_KHR_maintenance1.

Optional VK_KHR_synchronization2 with VkPhysicalDeviceSynchronization2FeaturesKHR::synchronization2 chained after the 1.2 features. It switches NVRHI's barriers to vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 (nvrhi vulkan-state-tracking.cpp:345), so the preview takes the game's barrier path. Dropped when the extension is listed but the feature is not.
Optional VK_EXT_memory_budget, the VRAM budget's source (S9, LP2).

VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures: shaderImageGatherExtended, samplerAnisotropy, textureCompressionBC, imageCubeArray, dualSrcBlend on; shaderStorageImageReadWithoutFormat, tessellationShader, geometryShader, fillModeNonSolid as supported. The five forced features are checked at device choice (the engine checks only samplerAnisotropy and textureCompressionBC there; the others would fail vkCreateDevice).

pickPhysicalDevice: per device the required extensions, features, B8G8R8A8_UNORM surface format, FIFO and present support; the first discrete GPU, else the first other device, in enumeration order. Added: Vulkan 1.2 or newer (S12), and the error text lists every device with its problems instead of FatalError. Changed: the surface's formats and present modes are asked only of a device with a family that presents to the surface, as the specification requires, and a device whose queries throw is skipped with a log line instead of ending the choice (review L3.3).

findQueueFamilies and the queue create infos. The engine takes the first graphics family and the first present family separately and may create two queues; the preview requires one family that does both, creates one queue and keeps the swapchain images exclusive.
Timer queries only when timestampPeriod > 0 and the family's timestampValidBits > 0; otherwise the frame log's GPU column stays empty.

nvrhi::vulkan::DeviceDesc with the enabled instance and device extensions, graphics queue only; nvrhi::validation::createValidationLayer in Debug with SessionOptions::validation (the engine: r_useValidationLayers). errorCB is the session's own callback, which counts errors and sets the lost flag (R5.19), instead of DefaultMessageCallback, which turns errors into FatalError.
Swapchain format RGBA8_UNORM swapped to B8G8R8A8_UNORM. The engine always pairs it with SRGB_NONLINEAR; the preview takes the colour space of the surface's matching format entry.
Swapchain image count NUM_FRAME_DATA = 3, clamped to the surface's minImageCount and maxImageCount (0 = no limit).

entries.note: VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR: usage ColorAttachment | TransferDst | Sampled, one array layer, identity pre-transform, opaque composite alpha, clipped, no old swapchain. The preview falls back to the current transform and the first supported alpha mode when identity or opaque is not offered, and always uses exclusive sharing (one family).
Swapchain image wrappers: createHandleForNativeTexture(VK_Image) with initialState Present, keepInitialState, isRenderTarget.

The engine clamps its back-buffer size into the surface's range. The preview uses currentExtent, takes the passed window size only when currentExtent is 0xFFFFFFFF, and makes no swapchain for 0×0 (§3.1).

The engine's r_swapInterval / r_vkPreferFastSync choice among MAILBOX, IMMEDIATE, FIFO_RELAXED and FIFO. The preview uses MAILBOX if offered, else FIFO, and FIFO when forced (D48, R5.4); IMMEDIATE only if LP0 measures FIFO's present blocking beyond a bound.

The engine acquires with an infinite timeout and asserts on the result, and cycles one semaphore per image for both acquire and present. The preview acquires with a 50 ms timeout (D48) through the vk::Result overloads, skips on TIMEOUT or NOT_READY, posts SwapchainOutOfDate on OUT_OF_DATE or SUBOPTIMAL, and keeps acquire semaphores per frame in flight and present semaphores per image, all owned by the swapchain generation.

The engine's single frame event query, waited per NUM_FRAME_DATA. The preview keeps a ring of kFramesInFlight event queries and waits on frame N - 2's before recording frame N (D35). The wait polls the event query and ends on a stop or a park, where NVRHI's waitEventQuery would wait without a bound (review L2.1).

Optional device extensions and features the preview does not need: VK_EXT_debug_marker (debug utils replaces it), VK_EXT_descriptor_indexing (its features are core 1.2 and enabled through VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features), VK_KHR_buffer_device_address and bufferDeviceAddress (ray tracing only; the engine notes it 'only makes problems'), VK_NV_mesh_shader, VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate and its features, VK_KHR_format_feature_flags2, VK_GOOGLE_display_timing and hostQueryReset (Optick), the ray-tracing extensions, the macOS portability subset.

Instance extensions: VK_KHR_get_physical_device_properties2 (core since 1.1; the instance is 1.2), VK_EXT_sampler_filter_minmax (listed by the engine as an instance extension, but it is a device extension and its feature is never enabled), VK_EXT_debug_report and its callback (replaced by VK_EXT_debug_utils, which Qt adds for its debug output redirect when the session validates; the tests' own instance asks for it itself). Qt adds the surface extensions.
The VK_LAYER_MESSAGE_ID_FILTER environment variable: a process-wide setting; LP0 creates no pipelines, whose warnings it filters. Revisit when pipelines arrive (LP2).
The D24S8 format probe, the VMA allocator, the push-constant size and Optick's GPU init: not used by LP0. The push-constant size and the depth format come with the passes (LP2, C2).
Compute and transfer queues: the preview submits everything, uploads included, on the graphics queue (S35).

The engine's destruction order (waitIdle, semaphores, swapchain, device handle, VkDevice, surface, instance) never collects NVRHI garbage. The preview follows §3.1's teardown steps instead: release handles, waitForIdle, runGarbageCollection (skipped when lost), wrappers, vkDestroySwapchainKHR, semaphores, the NVRHI device with its last Release() count, then the VkDevice; the surface and the instance belong to Qt.

entries.note: ParseStage warns at the 257th stage but does not return, and writes past pd->parseStages[256] on the parse thread's stack (A2.4; the engine at the pinned commit has the same defect). After numStages++ it also writes a coverage stage at parseStages[numStages] with no limit check when the stage is diffuse and alpha-tested (engine Material.cpp:2298-2302, the copy's 2299-2303), so one call can write two slots. Before anything can parse it, every material decl whose text can make more than 256 slots is made the default material, with the engine's warning, and its lookup fails with that reason. The bound comes from the copied idLexer's tokens with DECL_LEXER_FLAGS (forEachDeclToken, the tokens idMaterial::Parse reads): after the first "{" (SkipUntilString), every token equal to "{" counts 1 and every stage shortcut keyword 2, whatever its type and wherever it stands. ParseMaterial calls ParseStage only for such a token, once per token. A stage is diffuse only through ParseBlend's diffusemap or basecolormap: in a "{" block that is a token of the material's text, counted 2, which pays for the block's coverage slot; a shortcut's stage is parsed from synthesised text holding its image name without the quotes (AppendToken), so diffusemap "_white alphaTest 0.5" makes two slots that its second count pays for. AddImplicitStages adds at most one stage, below the limit, without an alpha test. So the bound is never below the slots the engine writes; it is above them where such a token is an argument, a block's own keyword or text after a parse error (M-ID-DIFF-03). W.1 (round 2) replaced a character scan of brace depth that crafted text got past ('diffusemap {', 'qer_editorimage {', the lexer's '/*/' comment, '.5diffusemap'); X.1 (round 3) counts shortcuts twice for the coverage stage

The tokens are the copied idLexer's with DECL_LEXER_FLAGS over the whole file (forEachDeclToken, which silences only the lexer's printing with LEXFL_NOERRORS and LEXFL_NOWARNINGS and goes on after a token it cannot read wherever the lexer moved forward; the decl parsers go on there too, while LoadAndParse stops at a failed top-level read, so the scan reads a superset of the tokens the engine reads), so strings joined across a backslash, '...' literals with spaces, a name after a number and the lexer's comment rules are read exactly as the engine reads them; tokens inside comments are not tokens. What a read of the path finds, in C8's order, without opening a file body: a loose file's time is Sys_FileTimeStamp's, on Windows (GetFileAttributesExW's last write ticks - 116444736000000000) / 10^7 with C++'s truncation, on POSIX stat's st_mtime; a .pk4 or .resources entry has time 0, looked up in the tables read at construction; no file has FILE_NOT_FOUND_TIMESTAMP (-1). A link is followed to its file, as the engine's open follows it. The change stamp (FILETIME ticks) is kept beside it for polling only

A5 (LP1c.1): the engine's time-only ReadFile opens the file and returns its length; the probe opens nothing, so a .pk4 entry's length, which only inflating it tells, is 0 (no copied caller reads the length of a time-only call: the loaders return at once). A loose file that can be statted but not opened is found by the probe and missed by a read, which goes on to the containers

LP1c.1, for the loaders LP1c.2 copies: OpenFileRead reads the file whole through the source's C8 search (readGameFile) and serves it from memory as idFile_Memory does (Read copies at most the bytes left and moves past them), with the time the search found: a loose file's Unix seconds, as idFile_Permanent::Timestamp gives them, 0 in a container. The game file is closed once read (R4-3.26); CloseFile frees the object. Null for no file, a file of 2 GB or more, and once the registry's cancel flag is set. Minimal: only GetFullPath, Read, Length and Timestamp exist (M-ID-VIRT-12). LP1c.2: the copied loaders read with ReadFile, never OpenFileRead (LoadTGA, LoadSTB_RGBA8, LoadEXR and LoadHDR call ReadFile with a buffer), so BufferedFile needed nothing more (LP1c.1's follow-up 4) and OpenFileRead has no copied caller; it stays for idFile's callers to come

§3.7 (LP1c.1), not in the engine: the area counts of the files that exist must agree: the grid names each area once and as many areas as the tree has, every SH probe's area is -1 or below the count; a mismatch drops the grid and the probes (no-bake behaviour) with the reason, and keeps the tree (the newest dmap's). Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the image type is 2, 3 or 10 (tgaProblem)

the colour map is not skipped: the decoder reads the colour map's bytes as pixels, and the image data past them runs off the buffer's end. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the colour map type is 0 (tgaProblem)

the size check uses pixel_size >> 3; the uncompressed loop reports 298 per pixel without advancing, the RLE loop 337/389 per packet, so the picture keeps uninitialised or stale pixels. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the pixel size is 24 or 32, or 8, 24 or 32 for a grey image (tgaProblem)

the decoder reads numBytes from a buffer that holds fewer: it reads past the end of the file's buffer. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the declared size fits the bytes after the header and comment (tgaProblem)

Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the pixel size is one the uncompressed decoder reads (tgaProblem)

the run writes the previous packet's colour packetSize times. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the run-length decoder only meets 24 or 32 bits (tgaProblem)

the pixel is not written but counted, so it stays uninitialised. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the run-length decoder only meets 24 or 32 bits (tgaProblem)

frees tinyexr's message and returns without a picture; R_LoadImage tries the other extensions. The file's buffer is not freed on this path (M-IMG-DEFECT-01). Reachable only for a file that passes the pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01: tinyexr's header parse, one channel or R, G and B, a scanline image's offset table and blocks inside the file) and whose data tinyexr then refuses (a corrupt compressed block, a tiled file cut short)

with a picture of 1 or 2 channels (a non-Radiance file stb_image loads as LDR) the conversion reads 3 floats per pixel past the end of stb's buffer; with no picture numChannels is read uninitialised. entries.note: LoadEXR returns after a failed LoadEXRFromMemory without Mem_Free( fbuffer ): the file's buffer leaks once per such file and load. Kept verbatim (C7); the pre-validation makes it rare, and the shim's buffers are plain Mem_Alloc blocks

entries.reason: a constant-initialised table of extensions and function pointers, and its count; never written

stb_image's globals are constant-initialised: the failure reason is thread_local and written by each failing call on its own thread; the flip, unpremultiply and iPhone-conversion flags and the gamma and scale are written only by their setter functions, which nothing calls. Every load runs on the parse thread (C20)
a non-const float[256] initialised from literals (constant initialisation), only read by R_MipMapWithGamma; the cmft tables of 854-1167 are static const

entries.note: LP1c.2 (D51, R5.3, C17): every file a copied loader reads is validated outside the copied code before the loader sees it. The file system, between beginImageReads and endImageReads (MaterialDecls::loadImagePixels), reads it through the source's readGameFile and hands the loader nothing (-1, no buffer, FILE_NOT_FOUND_TIMESTAMP) for a file that fails, keeping the refusal once per path; a stop reads every image file as missing, never as an empty buffer. The checks follow each loader's reads: TGA - the 18-byte header, type 2, 3 or 10, no colour map, 24 or 32 bits (8 too for grey), the declared size of an uncompressed image against the bytes after the header and comment, the RLE packets walked as the decoder walks them up to the last pixel; PNG - stb_image's header rules (signature, a 13-byte IHDR first, depth 1/2/4/8/16, colour type 0/2/3/4/6, 16-bit palettes refused, methods 0, interlace 0 or 1, PLTE before IDAT for a palette, unknown critical chunks), every chunk inside the file up to IEND, and the declared pixels within 1032 bytes per IDAT byte (deflate's limit); JPG - SOI, every marker segment inside the file, a baseline or progressive 8-bit frame of 1, 3 or 4 components with sampling 1-4 and tables 0-3, each scan's entropy-coded bytes walked to the next marker, EOI reached, and at most 8 blocks per scan byte (a block of the finest component costs at least one Huffman bit); EXR - tinyexr's ParseEXRVersionFromMemory and ParseEXRHeaderFromMemory, single part and not deep, one channel or R, G and B (what LoadEXRFromMemory needs), for a scanline image the offset table and every block inside the file; HDR - stb_image's identifier, header with FORMAT=32-bit_rle_rgbe, '-Y h +X w' line, and every pixel byte stb_image reads (flat, run-length scanlines, the flat fallback), so stb_image always decodes it to three channels. Every size: at least 1, at most 16384 a side and 8192 x 8192 in all (M-IMG-DIFF-04). An empty file fails. Tested with truncated, 16-bit, RLE-garbage and oversized TGAs, a PNG with a lying IHDR, a 0-byte file and JPGs cut short or with a 4096 x 4096 header over one block of scan data (tst_ImageFiles.cpp)

Before the copied R_LoadCubeImages runs for a CF_SINGLE image with a cube size, the picture is loaded as it loads it (R_LoadImageProgram, no usage) and a smaller one is refused: the image is the default, with a warning. engine.anchor: ActuallyLoadImage, the source load and its DeriveOpts

entries.note: LP1c.2 (S14, D24, A3): the source fallback. Where the engine would binarize (no cache, or one resolveImageCache calls Stale) the copied loaders read the source (M-IMG-08) and the levels are what Load2DFromMemory or LoadCubeFromMemory hands its encoder with image_highQualityCompression 0: the 2D colour conversion (YCoCg through the copied idColorSpace::ConvertRGBToCoCg_Y for CFM_YCOCG_DXT5; the fast normal-map swizzle x -> alpha, red and blue 0 for CFM_NORMAL_DXT5; alpha -> green for CFM_GREEN_ALPHA), DXT5's colour format forced to CFM_DEFAULT when neither, the mip chain through the copied R_MipMapR11G11B10F (BC6H, R11G11B10F), R_MipMapWithGamma (gammaMips) or R_MipMap, each level stored as the engine stores an uncompressed format (RGB565 high byte first, then expanded with the cache reader's Option 1; LUM8/INT8 red, ALPHA, L8A8, RG16F, R11G11B10F, RGBA8 for anything else) or as the encoder's RGBA8 input (DXT1, DXT5) or R11G11B10F input (BC6H: the SSE build encodes it). A cube: no conversion, CFM_DEFAULT, the records in the engine's images[ level * 6 + side ] order. Format, colour format and gamma mips are DeriveOpts' for the usage the time call found (a program's pixel path may turn the usage TD_BUMP afterwards, which changes nothing, as in the engine); the mip count is DeriveOpts' for the picture's size and the key's filter. The result is a CachedImage tagged fromSource, published in the image's slot; MaterialService::image answers Ready (cache), Source (fallback), Generated (intrinsic) or Default. Differences: M-IMG-DIFF-05

LP1c.2 (D24, D11): the fallback stops before the encoder: no BC1, BC3 or BC6H on the CPU, so its levels are RGBA8 where the cache holds DXT1 or DXT5 blocks and R11G11B10F where it holds BC6H (the engine accepts R11G11B10F for BC6H, SC99); its 2D levels are unpadded, where the engine pads a DXT level with zeros to whole 4 x 4 blocks, and a cube level below 4 x 4 keeps its size, where the engine replicates it into one block and records 4 x 4. It writes no cache file (the engine binarizes and writes one): the image is made again per session and on a source change. Image arrays and packed mip chains (engine-made bakes) and the editor's own image are never made from a source

engine.anchor: idImage::ActuallyLoadImage (the cache's size, the source's, the 8 x 8 default)

entries.note: LP1c.2 (C21, A6, P.4, P.11): MaterialEntry::editorImageSize is GetEditorImage's upload size, measured on the parse thread when the entry is published (sized, LP1b.0's hook), silently (the copied code's messages while it measures are dropped). The chain: qer_editorimage's key as ImageFromFile names and finds it with TF_DEFAULT, TR_REPEAT, TD_DIFFUSE (the default image for an empty or default name, the fonts and lights usages, the extensions stripped, an existing record), without making a record; when its load is defaulted, the first SL_DIFFUSE stage's image or stage 0's when that one has none, but the defaulted editor image when no stage is diffuse; without qer_editorimage the first SL_DIFFUSE stage's image, else stage 0's; no stage or no image: the default image. An image's size: the default image and the fixed-size intrinsics by their generators (16 x 16 for _default, _white, _black, _flat, ...; _quadratic 32 x 4; window-, cvar- and font-sized ones unknown, Default); else the time call names the cache, and a cache the engine would use (not stale, matching DeriveOpts, the BFHACK name too) gives its header's size, read with readGameFileHead (36 bytes, not the body); else the source: a single image's file, the one the copied R_LoadImage's leaf resolution found in the time call (the .tga default, png/tga/jpg/exr/hdr, the _rmao sibling), sized by its header when the loader pre-validation passes it (imageFileHeader); a program or a cube through the copied loaders, quietly (a program by its first leaf; addnormals resamples its second to the first's size); a load that fails or a missing source is the engine's defaulted 8 x 8. Ready is a size the engine uploads; Default is the defaulted 8 x 8 or an unknown size, with the reason. A Ready size is kept per canonical name across reloads (D52). The LP1b fixture's six editor images equal the engine's listImages, from the caches' headers and from the sources' alike (tst_EditorImageSize.cpp)

LP1c.2 (C21): the engine loads an image once per level and again on reloadImages; the preview re-reads on its 1 s poll: the loose files each published editor-image size and each image slot was read from, or that the time call found, are probed (no body read), and one whose time, size or change stamp changed makes the slot read again (resolveImage) and the material's size measured again, its kept Ready size dropped so that the new size or the loss of the file is published under every name that shares the entry. Files in containers are not polled (their tables are read once). A Ready size that changes to another Ready size reaches the chunks only when they are rebuilt for another reason: SceneGeometry rebuilds provisional (Default) chunks when their size turns Ready (a follow-up)

LP1c.2 (C21): a single source image is sized by its header, never decoded: a file that passes the loader pre-validation but that stb_image or tinyexr then fails to decode (corrupt compressed data) is Ready at its header's size here and the engine's defaulted 8 x 8 there. An intrinsic the engine sizes by its window, a cvar or a font atlas (_currentRender, _shadowMapAtlas, _imguiFont, ...) is Default here. GetEditorImage's record is never made, so listImages-like listings of the registry do not show editor images the engine's dmap would have loaded
